prompt: Match each part of southamerica-east1-docker.pkg.dev/planner-dev/shop/web:1.4.0 to what it is.
hint: Read it left to right like a path.

pairs.right: The project that owns and pays

prompt: A Cloud Run service in São Paulo pulls from a repository in Iowa. What does that cost the shop?
hint: The region is part of the host.

choices.text: Nothing; pulls between Google regions are free
choices.why: Data crossing regions is billed.

choices.text: A second copy of the storage charge
choices.why: Storage is billed once, where it is stored.

choices.text: Data transfer between regions, and a slower pull at every cold start
choices.why: Right. Keep the repository beside what pulls from it.

choices.text: The pull is refused across regions
choices.why: It works; it costs and waits.

prompt: Which repository mode keeps builds working when Docker Hub limits the shop's pulls?
hint: A cache in front of an upstream.

choices.text: remote
choices.why: Right. It fetches on the first pull and serves its copy afterwards.

choices.text: standard
choices.why: Standard stores what you push; it fetches nothing.

choices.text: virtual
choices.why: Virtual combines repositories; on its own it caches nothing.

choices.text: immutable
choices.why: That is a tag setting, not a mode.

prompt: The plan printed mode = "STANDARD_REPOSITORY". Where did it come from?
hint: It was not in the file.

choices.text: Google's API, asked during the plan
choices.why: The plan asked no API.

choices.text: The format DOCKER, which forces it
choices.why: Docker repositories can be remote or virtual too.

choices.text: The project's organisation policy
choices.why: Nothing of the organisation was read.

choices.text: The provider's default
choices.why: Right. A repository is standard unless you say otherwise.

prompt: Artifact Registry charges 0.10 USD per GiB-month after the first 0.5 GiB. What does 12.5 GiB stored for a month cost?
hint: Subtract the free half GiB first.

prompt: What did gcloud auth configure-docker change on the laptop?
hint: jq showed the file.

choices.text: It stored an access token in ~/.docker/config.json
choices.why: No token or password is stored.

choices.text: One credHelpers entry naming gcloud for that host
choices.why: Right. Docker asks gcloud for a token at each push.

choices.text: It logged Docker in to Google with the project's key
choices.why: There is no project key, and nothing logged in.

choices.text: It installed a new version of Docker
choices.why: It only edited a file.

prompt: Why does plain docker push work against Artifact Registry at all?
hint: The same protocol as the local registry.

choices.text: Google ships a patched Docker in the gcloud CLI
choices.why: It is the ordinary Docker.

choices.text: Artifact Registry converts Docker's format on arrival
choices.why: Nothing is converted; the protocol is shared.

choices.text: It speaks the OCI Distribution protocol like every registry
choices.why: Right. That is why the local registry could stand in for the protocol.

choices.text: docker push uploads through gcloud
choices.why: gcloud only supplies the token.

prompt: Which of these does the local registry:3.1.2 NOT show faithfully?
hint: It has no permissions, scanning or policies.

choices.text: Who is allowed to push
choices.why: Right. It has no IAM; anybody on the laptop can push.

choices.text: What a push uploads
choices.why: The protocol is the same.

choices.text: That the answer to a push is a digest
choices.why: Every registry answers with the digest.

choices.text: How tags and digests relate
choices.why: Section 04 showed that on it.

prompt: The program Docker runs to get a token for southamerica-east1-docker.pkg.dev is docker-credential-___.
hint: It came with the Google Cloud command line.

prompt: A build server must push to Artifact Registry. What does the lesson recommend instead of a long-lived password?
hint: No person logs in there.

choices.text: A JSON key file copied to the server
choices.why: That is the long-lived secret the helper avoids.

choices.text: A personal access token of one developer
choices.why: It ties builds to one person's account.

choices.text: Making the repository public for the duration of the build
choices.why: Public is for reading; it would not let anyone push.

choices.text: The credential helper with the server's service account
choices.why: Right. Tokens are short-lived, and Cloud Build needs nothing at all.

prompt: After tagging 1.4.0 as latest and pushing, what did the registry report for the two tags?
hint: Nothing new was stored.

choices.text: Two different digests, one per tag
choices.why: Both tags pointed at the same bytes.

choices.text: The same digest for both
choices.why: Right. latest was a second name for the same image.

choices.text: An error, because latest is reserved
choices.why: latest is an ordinary tag.

choices.text: A digest only for 1.4.0
choices.why: Both answered with a digest.

prompt: After the second build, which tag still pointed at the first digest?
hint: One tag was not pushed again.

choices.text: latest
choices.why: latest moved to the new image.
1.4.1 named the new image from the start.
Right. Nobody pushed it again, so it did not move.

choices.text: None of them
choices.why: 1.4.0 stayed where it was.

prompt: A service deployed as web:latest on Monday is restarted on Wednesday and behaves differently, with no change to its configuration. What happened?
hint: A tag is a pointer.

choices.text: Someone pushed a new latest, and the restart pulled it
choices.why: Right. Deploy by digest and this cannot happen.

choices.text: The registry corrupted the image
choices.why: A digest check would have caught corruption.

choices.text: Docker caches latest for 48 hours
choices.why: No such rule; the tag moved.

choices.text: The base image auto-updated inside the container
choices.why: A running image never changes itself.

prompt: The repository setting that refuses a push moving an existing tag is ___ tags.
hint: Its name says they cannot change.

prompt: A version matches both keep-recent and delete-old. What happens to it?
hint: One kind of policy is applied first.

choices.text: It is deleted, because DELETE is more specific
choices.why: Specificity does not decide; keep wins.

choices.text: The plan fails with a conflict
choices.why: The plan was clean with both.

choices.text: It is moved to an archive repository
choices.why: Cleanup keeps or deletes; it moves nothing.

choices.text: It is kept, because keep policies win
choices.why: Right. The ten newest survive even past thirty days.

prompt: older_than = "2592000s". How many days is that?
hint: A day is 86,400 seconds.

prompt: Why does Google recommend running a new cleanup policy as a dry run first?
hint: What is hard to undo?

choices.text: Dry runs are free and real runs are billed
choices.why: Cost is not the reason given.

choices.text: It logs what would go, before a policy deletes what production runs
choices.why: Right. A deleted image is the mistake that is hard to undo.

choices.text: A real run locks the repository for a day
choices.why: No such lock.

choices.text: Terraform cannot plan a policy without one
choices.why: The plan above had none.

prompt: What does vulnerability scanning compare?
hint: Packages against advisories.

choices.text: Your code against a list of insecure patterns
choices.why: It does not read your code.

choices.text: Two images, to see what changed
choices.why: That is a diff, not a scan.

choices.text: The image's packages against published advisories
choices.why: Right. A known flaw becomes a named finding.

choices.text: Running containers against a firewall
choices.why: It reads images, not traffic.

prompt: Which of these can a vulnerability scan NOT see? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three things the lesson names.

choices.text: A secret copied into a layer
choices.why: Right; it reads packages, not configuration.

choices.text: A flaw nobody has published yet
choices.why: Right; it compares against advisories.

choices.text: A bug in the shop's own code
choices.why: Right; it does not read your code.

choices.text: An outdated package with a published advisory
choices.why: That is exactly what it finds.

prompt: Which reduction in findings does the lesson call the cheapest?
hint: Before any scan.

choices.text: A smaller base image
choices.why: Right. Fewer packages, fewer findings.

choices.text: Suppressing low-severity findings
choices.why: That hides them; it removes nothing.

choices.text: Scanning less often
choices.why: The flaws stay; you just see them later.

choices.text: Deploying by tag rather than digest
choices.why: That does not change the packages.

prompt: A critical finding is in a package the web image contains but never loads. What is the right first response, by this lesson?
hint: Ask the three questions.

choices.text: Stop the service until the scan is clean
choices.why: Severity alone does not decide urgency.

choices.text: Ignore it permanently, since it is unused
choices.why: A smaller base or an update still removes it.

choices.text: Turn off automatic scanning for the repository
choices.why: That hides every future finding too.

choices.text: Check reachability and a fixed version, and plan the fix by that
choices.why: Right. Unused and unreachable is noise; a smaller base removes it.

prompt: Put the release of web 1.4.1 to Cloud Run in a safe order.
hint: Build, push, check, deploy what you checked.
items: Build the image and tag it 1.4.1
Push it to the shop repository
Read the scan findings for that digest
Deploy by the digest the push returned

prompt: The shop turns on immutable tags. What must its pipeline stop doing?
hint: One tag is pushed again on every build.

choices.text: Pushing version tags such as 1.4.1
choices.why: A new version tag is a new tag; it is allowed.

choices.text: Pushing latest on every build
choices.why: Right. Moving latest is exactly what is refused.

choices.text: Deploying by digest
choices.why: Digests are the recommendation.

choices.text: Running cleanup policies
choices.why: Cleanup works with immutable tags.
